analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md head lines 1751-1753 add three rows to the LaunchAgent environment passthrough table for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. Each row points to a source file and constant: GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, and EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift (two keys). The table sits under the sentence that `darkbloom start` copies 'only these variables' from the shell into the plist EnvironmentVariables. No code, endpoint, coordinator contract, key handling, attestation or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct regression. I examined the three base units (4-6) against the threat model. Relevant threats are T-041 (prefix-cache/TTFT oracle, SEC-035), T-028 (residual GPU memory), T-011/T-014 (memory exposure) and TB-007.

Unverified contract: the new names suggest TTFT, idle cache sweep, segment retention and host-zeros behavior in the KV/segmented backend. I could not see the Swift sources, so I cannot confirm whether the new knobs change retention of KV data or cache residency (T-028, T-041). The doc does not describe their semantics, defaults or whether they can only tighten behavior. If the corresponding code changes shipped in the same PR, the next pass should check whether SEGMENT_RETENTION extends how long decrypted KV data stays in memory, whether IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP affects residual-memory clearing, and whether the passthrough (a shell env var persisted into the launchd plist) creates a way to weaken the cache-purge or isolation posture. The T-041 sign-off ties the cache reuse window to the 30-minute TTL and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. Because the supplied evidence shows no behavior change, I make no finding and ask only for confirmation of the code behind these keys. The edit also does not state that the keys are inference-tuning only, and it leaves the 'only these variables' sentence unchanged.
